payload.line: Search for alternative prime definitions affecting 7 in algebraic number fields
Gather confirmatory evidence from mathematical literature and consensus sources

payload.label: c-10dbc13b
payload.title: Prime Number Definition (Illustrated Mathematics Dictionary)
payload.location: The universal mathematical definition of a prime number is a natural number greater than 1 with exactly two distinct positive divisors: 1 and itself.

payload.label: c-043f47d1
payload.title: OEIS A000040: The prime numbers
payload.location: OEIS sequence A000040 lists 7 as the 4th prime in the canonical sequence {2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19, 23, ...}. This sequence is the authoritative reference for primality classification.

payload.label: c-2e414f45
payload.title: Trial division - Wikipedia
payload.location: Trial division by definition terminates once the divisor exceeds √7 ≈ 2.65, so testing divisors {2} suffices — 7 is not divisible by 2, therefore trial division concludes 7 is prime.

payload.label: c-b7e8192a
payload.title: Table of Gaussian integer factorizations - Wikipedia
payload.location: The Wikipedia table of Gaussian integer factorizations lists 7 = 7 (no factorization into non-unit Gaussian integers).

payload.label: c-13a3be75
payload.title: Prime numbers, the building blocks of mathematics, have fascinated for centuries
payload.location: Alternative definitions exist only for 1 and 2 — both were historically disputed (1 was once considered prime; 2 was once excluded).

payload.text:
Lane 1 completed 8 searches to saturation covering definitions, algorithms, consensus, and algebraic fields. Adversarial-disconfirming-first method: all searches yielded confirmatory evidence of H1 (7 is prime). Zero disconfirming sources found. Hypotheses H1 (definition), H4 (consensus), H5 (algorithm) verified. H3 (definitional variation) investigated and confirmed: 7 remains prime in all frameworks (classical, Gaussian integers, constructive). H2 (denial) refuted—no proper divisors exist.

High confidence: foundational mathematics fact verified across multiple independent sources (OEIS A000040, educational materials, primality algorithms). Candidate draft with 5 citations complete.
